source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Gather comprehensive data: Collect accurate and detailed information from monitoring equipment, such as air quality monitors and emissions tracking devices, that measure pollutants, like particulate matter (PM10, PM2.5), nitrogen oxides (NOx), sulfur dioxide (SO2), carbon monoxide (CO), and volatile organic compounds (VOCs).

Specify locations and time-frames: Clearly document the geographic coordinates of the source, the date, and the time of measurement. This ensures the recorded data can be corroborated with weather conditions and other local events.

Detail the measurement methods: Describe the types of gas analyzers used, such as infrared spectroscopy or electrochemical sensors, and reference their calibration certificates and maintenance logs. This establishes the credibility of your findings.

Cross-reference with industry benchmarks: Compare the recorded emissions with the standards allowed by law, and with industry-specific benchmarks. Document any deviations.

Include wind and weather data: Incorporate meteorological data, such
